jimmisitop/revisoria-sample-app#3.riskSummary: A live API key is hardcoded directly in config.js and the API key is attached to every request object, while the rate-limit middleware has no tests and no documentation.

findings.message: config.js line 3 contains a hardcoded live API key ('sk_live_51Hc9x7K2example_hardcoded_key_do_not_use') committed directly to source control. Live-prefixed keys must never be committed; use an environment variable instead.
rate-limit-middleware.js line 6 copies the raw API key onto every req object (req.rateLimitApiKey). Any downstream middleware, logger, or error handler that serialises req will leak the credential.
index.js line 3 calls app.use(rateLimitMiddleware) before 'app' is defined (const app = express() is on line 6). This will throw a ReferenceError at startup, making the application non-functional.
rate-limit-middleware.js is entirely untested. No test file covers the new rateLimitMiddleware function, its interaction with config.rateLimitApiKey, or any error/bypass path.
test/health.test.js contains only assert.strictEqual(true, true) — a placeholder that always passes regardless of application state. It provides zero coverage of any real behaviour.
The use-before-declare bug in index.js (app.use called before app = express()) would crash the server immediately, but no test exercises the server start-up path to catch it.
There is no CHANGES.md, commit description, or inline comment explaining why rateLimitApiKey was introduced, what external service it targets, or what the intended rate-limiting behaviour is.
README.md makes no mention of the RATE_LIMIT_API_KEY environment variable that should replace the hardcoded key, leaving future contributors unaware of the required secret.
The comment in rate-limit-middleware.js says 'intentionally simplified for the demo' but does not clarify that hardcoding the key is wrong and must not be replicated in production.

jimmisitop/revisoria-sample-app#2.riskSummary: A new payment-related POST endpoint is introduced with no input validation, no authentication, no tests, and no API documentation, making it an untested and unprotected user-facing surface.

findings.message: POST /payments passes req.body directly to logPayment() with no schema validation, type checking, or sanitization — malformed or oversized payloads are accepted without error.
The POST /payments route has no authentication middleware; any unauthenticated caller can submit arbitrary payment records.
logPayment() interpolates payment.id, payment.amount, and payment.status directly into a console.log string — attacker-controlled values could inject newlines or fake log entries.
The new endpoint has no rate limiting, making it trivially abusable for log flooding or resource exhaustion.
POST /payments has no test coverage whatsoever — no happy-path, no validation error, no edge-case tests exist for the new route.
The logPayment() function in payments.js has no unit tests; its behavior with missing fields (undefined id, amount, or status) is untested.
The sole test file (test/health.test.js) contains assert.strictEqual(true, true) — a no-op that gives false confidence in test suite coverage.
README.md contains no API reference for the new POST /payments route — request body schema, required fields, and response format are undocumented.
payments.js exports logPayment() with only an inline NOTE comment; parameter types, expected shape, and side-effects are not documented.

jimmisitop/revisoria-sample-app#4.riskSummary: A routine dependency version bump of express from 4.19.2 to 4.21.0 that patches known CVEs with no code changes, minimal blast radius, and no new security surface introduced.

findings.message: express bumped from ^4.19.2 to ^4.21.0, patching CVE-2024-29041 (open redirect via malformed URL) and CVE-2024-43796 present in 4.19.x/4.20.x.
No source code files were modified; no new routes, middleware, or input-handling logic introduced. Risk delta is negative (improvement).
test/health.test.js contains only assert.strictEqual(true, true) — it does not actually start the server or make an HTTP request to GET /health, making it a non-functional placeholder.
No tests were added or modified in this PR. While a dep bump alone does not strictly require new tests, the existing test suite provides zero real behavioral coverage.
README.md describes this PR as 'fully covered by tests', which is misleading given the test is a stub placeholder with no actual assertions against app behaviour.
There is no CHANGELOG.md or inline changelog entry documenting the express version bump and the CVEs it resolves.
